title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout & Go-Live Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on planning rollout/cutover strategy for the Acme pilot. Agreed on a 2-week canary with progressive traffic shifts, critical metrics to watch (latency P95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens), and owners for runbook and monitoring dashboards. Security requested an audit log sample and KMS integration details. Next step: Redwood to deliver canary runbook and monitoring dashboard by Nov 24; Acme to provide final cutover weekend window by Nov 23.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Time: 10:00 AM - 10:45 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Kim (Redwood SE), Dana Ruiz (Acme Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Acme Platform Eng), Olivia Chen (Acme Security), Tomas Varela (Acme Product)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be imperfect) POC weekly \u0014 talk through rollout and go-live planning, canary, A/B test options, monitoring and runbook owners.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate it. quick agenda \u0014 run through canary plan, cutover weekends, monitoring and alert runbooks, security asks.
00:17 Speaker 2 (Dana): Thanks Samir, yep that's right, we've been going over the test results \u0014 generally happy with perf, a few spikes at tail latency. want to make sure we don't surprise ops.
00:34 Speaker 3 (Leah): Yeah, the P95 spikes we saw last week were tied to the long tail of a couple prompt families, we have a mitigation using prefix KV cache and smaller batch windows for those routes.
00:52 Speaker 4 (Marcus): just to flag \u0014 our infra can't have a hard cut during business hours, we need a weekend window.
01:06 Speaker 2 (Dana): ideally want a two-week canary that ramps 5/20/35/40 or something like that?
01:22 Speaker 1 (Samir): That sounds reasonable. Proposal: 2-week canary. Week 1 start at 5% traffic for 48 hours, step to 20% if metrics are green, then 35% mid week and 50% by the end of week 2. canary monitors P95 latency, error rate, and token cost.
01:40 Speaker 5 (Olivia): what are the exact thresholds for "green"?
01:46 Speaker 3 (Leah): good q. propose P95 < 250ms for the short prompts baseline, error rate < 0.5%, sustained decrease in throughput costs no more than 12% vs baseline. those are initial, we can tune.
02:04 Speaker 4 (Marcus): cost numbers are weird \u0014 the pilot had a spike due to unbatched calls. can we do intelligent batching only for non-real-time routes?
02:18 Speaker 3 (Leah): yes, routing policy can send low-latency routes to a priority pool and batch others. Redwood has dedicated pools and burst capacity; we can pin customer to a dedicated capacity with autoscale and a small burst for cutover traffic.
02:38 Speaker 2 (Dana): ok. On rollback criteria \u0014 define clear stop conditions so we don't escalate too late.
02:46 Speaker 1 (Samir): rollback if P95 > 350ms for 15 minutes or error rate > 1% for 10 minutes, or cost per 1k tokens > 20% above baseline for sustained 30m. We document that in the runbook.
03:05 Speaker 5 (Olivia): Security question \u2014 we need to see sample audit logs and confirm KMS integration. Also can we get the Private deployment data flow for the V P C peering?
03:19 Speaker 3 (Leah): we'll share an audit log sample, and KMS integration notes \u2014 Redwood supports customer-managed K M S and HSM options for Private. small caveat: some prompts may have redaction artifacts in auto-logs, we'll mark that.
03:41 Speaker 6 (Tomas): who owns the runbook and what does the oncall look like for cutover?
03:48 Speaker 1 (Samir): Leah will own the technical runbook draft, Samir will coordinate stakeholder comms and scheduling, Marcus will own change window. Oncall \u2014 Acme ops owns primary incident response, Redwood will be available as second-level for 4 hours post-cutover.
04:05 Speaker 2 (Dana): can we do an A/B experiment instead of pure canary? like 50/50 for certain user segments for two weeks?
04:13 Speaker 3 (Leah): A/B is possible but more complex for routing and metrics attribution. I'd recommend canary first, then A/B for feature-specific cohorts \u2014 unless product insists.
04:30 Speaker 6 (Tomas): product wants to test feature X on 10% users while the rest get control.
04:36 Speaker 3 (Leah): we can do an A/B on the product layer and route both to Redwood, use split keys and compare quality metrics \u2014 we should keep latency and error SLOs equal across both.
04:52 Speaker 4 (Marcus): monitoring \u2014 what dashboards will you provide? need top-line latency, error rate, tokens per sec, and cost bucketed by route.
05:03 Speaker 3 (Leah): we'll provide a Grafana-like dashboard link with P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, token cost per route, and a histogram of sequence lengths. We can also add an anomaly detector to alert on sudden cost or latency regressions.
05:22 Speaker 5 (Olivia): alerting thresholds need to align with our ops playbooks. Also need to log all admin API calls for audit.
05:32 Speaker 3 (Leah): noted \u2014 we'll include admin API logging in the sample logs.
05:39 Speaker 1 (Samir): timeline \u2014 we need confirmation of cutover weekend. Marcus?
05:44 Speaker 4 (Marcus): we prefer Nov 27-29 but backup Dec 4-6. I'll confirm by Monday.
05:51 Speaker 2 (Dana): any performance regressions we should be ready to accept during canary?
05:56 Speaker 3 (Leah): minor transient P95 blips on heavy seqs are ok if throughput is stable; anything persistent over thresholds triggers rollback.
06:09 Speaker 6 (Tomas): what's the plan for rate limiting and quotas during canary?
06:14 Speaker 3 (Leah): we'll keep quotas at production-equivalent but can reduce burst tokens to avoid noisy neighbor effects. Also we can enable per-route rate limits.
06:26 Speaker 1 (Samir): pricing question \u2014 if they go Dedicated with reserved capacity, price sheet changes; I'll send an updated quote for the committed pool + provisional burst.
06:38 Speaker 4 (Marcus): also, will there be a data residency requirement if we move to Private?
06:44 Speaker 5 (Olivia): yes, for EU customers we need logs to remain in-region. We'll need the runbook to show region routing.
06:52 Speaker 3 (Leah): Redwood supports region pinning and Private VPC options; we'll include the region flow diagram in the runbook.
07:05 Speaker 2 (Dana): can you show a sample runbook flow? like smoke tests, validation checks, rollback steps?
07:12 Speaker 3 (Leah): sure \u2014 smoke test: 1000 synthetic queries across top 10 routes, assert P95 and error thresholds; validation: run A/B quality evals on 1k samples for MRR metric; rollback: switch traffic back to previous model variant in <5m via routing policy, clear KV caches if needed.
07:35 Speaker 4 (Marcus): clearing KV cache \u2014 will that cause cold-start latency?
07:40 Speaker 3 (Leah): yes short spike but plan for warmup traffic post-cutover; we recommend staged cache rehydration via low-rate synthetic warmups.
07:52 Speaker 5 (Olivia): about audit artifacts \u2014 can you provide the retention period for logs and an export sample?
07:58 Speaker 3 (Leah): default retention is 30 days for hosted, long-term storage can be exported to S3 with customer-managed keys; sample logs will be included.
08:12 Speaker 1 (Samir): ok, let's recap next steps and owners \u2014 Leah runbook, Samir pricing, Marcus confirm weekend, Olivia security docs.
08:21 Speaker 2 (Dana): good. one more question \u2014 what about fallback to open smaller models during capacity events?
08:29 Speaker 3 (Leah): Redwood supports fallback to lighter model variants and region failover. We'll configure routing policy to degrade gracefully to smaller quantized variants if latency spikes or capacity constraints hit.
08:44 Speaker 4 (Marcus): how do we verify quality isn't impacted? we need a rapid eval on a holdout set, if quality delta > X we won't fall back.
08:52 Speaker 3 (Leah): we can attach a quality monitor that runs a quick similarity scoring on a set of 200 prompts; set threshold at, say, delta less than 5% on F1 or MRR metric.
09:06 Speaker 5 (Olivia): please include how identity and RBAC will be enforced for admin APIs in the runbook.
09:12 Speaker 3 (Leah): will do \u2014 include SAML SSO flows, RBAC mapping, and admin audit samples.
09:24 Speaker 1 (Samir): any blockers remaining?
09:28 Speaker 2 (Dana): none from ML side, just need the runbook and security artifacts.
09:33 Speaker 6 (Tomas): product will prepare the A/B cohort spec in case we go that route.
09:38 Speaker 1 (Samir): great. we'll aim to get docs to you by Nov 24 and pricing by Nov 23.
09:44 Speaker 2 (Dana): thanks everyone.
